One of my favorite things to do is find hidden gems on Netflix. Here are a few with under 100,000 ratings on IMDb that I've come across in the past few years:

Never Let Me Go -- Heart shredding, bleak, dystopian young love film. Beautifully shot. This one will stay with you.

Let Me In -- Remake of a Scandinavian vampire film, but I actually liked this one better because of Chloe Grace-Moretz's performance.

It's Kind of a Funny Story -- Comedy. A mentally ill teenager is institutionalized and makes some crazy friends.

Centurion -- Sword and sandals action flick about a Roman officer stranded in pict-held Britain. Very violent, great action sequences. Excellent supporting performance by Dominic West. Fassbender is great, as always.

Beginners -- A man's mother dies, and his father admits that he's a homosexual. Can be a bit overserious, but amazing acting. Plummer is excellent, MacGregor is solid as always. This movie will make you fall in love with Melanie Laurent.

The American -- Incredibly atmospheric, very well shot spy thriller. Clooney is solid. Might be a bit plodding for some, it's definitely not an action film, but I loved it.

Animal Kingdom -- AMAZING Aussie crime film. I can't recommend it enough. Great writing, great acting. One of the best films on this entire list. See it ASAP.

Restrepo -- Jaw dropping documentary about a US airborne unit fighting in the Afghanistan mountains. Totally mind-blowing.

Haywire -- Great action sequences, very well shot. Nice ensemble cast. Thought it was terribly underrated.

Young Adult -- Another solid character study. Sad but funny. Excellent performance by Charlize Theron.

Win Win -- A wrestling coach takes care of a talented but waylaid youth who happens to be a wrestling prodigy. Funny, enjoyable movie.

Stuck In Love -- Romantic comedy about a divorced writer unable to give up his love for his ex-wife, and his children as they grow up and discover love for themselves.

Savages -- Two entrepreneurial marijuana dealers get tangled up in the Mexican drug underworld. This was released without much gossip but I thought it was pretty solid. Nice to see Oliver Stone showing signs of life.

Wanderlust -- A yuppie Manhattan couple stumble upon a hippie commune. Paul Rudd and Jennifer Aniston are both great.

The Five-Year Engagement -- A bit overlong, but Jason Segel is hilarious in the comedy about an engaged couple's rocky relationship. Chris Pratt and Alison Brie play great supporting roles.

Safety Not Guaranteed -- Quirky indie flick about a guy looking for help to time travel.

Bachelorette -- Basically a poor man's Bridesmaids. It only got middling reviews but I really enjoyed it.

The Iceman -- Story based on truth about a mob hitman who was considered an upstanding citizen and a family man before his arrest. I didn't enjoy the film all that much but I think it's very noteworthy because Michael Shannon is fucking amazing in it.

Thanks for Sharing -- A lighthearted indie comedy exploring addiction and its effects on people. Solid performances by Mark Ruffalo, Tim Robbins, and even Pink, which I believe is her debut role.

Smashed -- Indie about an elementary school teacher dealing with her alcoholism.

Oculus -- Solid horror flick featuring a girl who tries to outwit a haunted house.

The Spectacular Now -- Indie comedy that touches on the effects of alcoholism. A hard partying high school guy meets and falls for the prototypical nice girl.

Under The Skin -- Bizarre Indie horror flick. Total mind bender, very intelligent, doesn't hand feed you, expects you to decipher the film yourself. If you like movies like Upstream Color, Mulholland Drive, or shows like Twin Peaks, check this out. Scarlett Johansson is brilliant.

Palo Alto -- Coming of age weirdness when a girl's flirtations with her soccer coach get a little too serious.

Out of the Furnace -- Solid revenge flick starring Christian Bale.

Only God Forgives -- I'm honestly not sure if I love or hate this movie. Brilliantly shot but weighed down with a nonsensically dumb plot and paper thin characters.

Joe -- Didn't think Cage was as great as everyone said, but the kid was fantastic.

Drinking Buddies -- One of the few "mumblecore" films that clicks with me, thanks to the great performances.

It Follows -- Excellent old school-style horror film focused on suspense and unease rather than jump scares and gore.

Foxcatcher -- Two Olympians train with an eccentric billionaire. Thought Carrell was okay, but Ruffalo and Tatum were phenomenal. Really well shot, too.

That Awkward Moment -- Got really bad reviews but I found it hilarious.The three male leads are great, and Imogen Poots is a charm.

A Most Wanted Man -- Fantastic le Carre spy thriller. Astounding performance by Philip Seymour Hoffman.

The Drop -- Tense drama about two guys running a mob bar. Excellent performance by Tom Hardy. Cute dog.

St. Vincent -- Bill Murray being Bill Murray.

Son of a Gun -- Aussie crime drama. Ewan McGregor is great.

The Two Faces Of January -- Great thriller with strong performances. Viggo Mortensen is a consistently underrated actor.

Copenhagen -- Fascinating character study, solid performance by Renly Baratheon.

The One I Love -- Bizarre romantic comedy with a sci fi twist.

BONUS: Prisoners -- Not really overlooked, but such a phenomenal film I had to mention it. One of the best shot films of the past decade with amazing performances by Hugh Jackman, Jake Gyllenhaal, Viola Davis, Terrence Howard, Melissa Leo. Just a great overall film. It got excellent reviews but I still think people slept on how great the movie is. It's probably the best film I've seen overall in the past 5 years. Dennis Villeneuve (Director) and Roger Deakins (DP) are brilliant together, and I can't wait to see their next film Sicario later this year.
